pages.x: For five centuries the Khmer kings had ruled much of mainland Southeast Asia from Angkor, a vast city of temples and reservoirs in what is now Cambodia. Angkor Wat, built in the 1100s, is the largest religious monument in the world. But by the 1300s the empire was in decline.

In 1351 a Thai ruler, U Thong, founded a new capital on an island in the Chao Phraya River and named it Ayutthaya. Crowned as King Ramathibodi I, he gave his kingdom laws, and set out to win the western lands that had once been Angkor's. Standing on the trade routes to the sea, Ayutthaya grew rich fast.

According to the chronicles of Ayutthaya, the king's son, Prince Ramesuan, marched east and besieged Angkor around 1352, and the city fell after a long siege. The Khmer won their capital back within a few years, but the raid showed how weak they had become.

Ramesuan, now king, took Angkor again around 1394, the chronicles say, carrying off thousands of captives and setting a son on the Khmer throne. Once more the Khmer drove the Siamese out, but province after province was slipping away.

In 1431 King Borommarachathirat II of Ayutthaya besieged Angkor for months and took it. Its treasures, its Brahmin priests and dancers and many of its people were carried off to Ayutthaya, where Khmer court culture shaped the ceremonies of the Siamese kings for centuries.

The Khmer king, Ponhea Yat, judged Angkor too close to the Siamese, and moved his court south-east, in the end to Phnom Penh, where the Mekong and the Tonle Sap rivers meet. The temples of Angkor were left to the monks and the jungle.

Angkor was never quite forgotten: Buddhist monks kept Angkor Wat as a holy place. But when a French explorer, Henri Mouhot, described the ruins in the 1860s, Europeans thought they had found a lost city in the jungle, and Angkor became famous around the world.

Ayutthaya was the leading power of mainland Southeast Asia for four centuries, until the Burmese destroyed it in 1767. Cambodia, squeezed between Siam and Vietnam, never regained its old power, but Angkor Wat stands at the centre of its national flag.
pts: The Khmer moved to Phnom Penh
